_comment: Maps each framework library in seed_data/frameworks/ onto the SCF crosswalk. Data, not code: a new framework or a new SCF release is an edit here plus a re-seed. `expected` is a drift tripwire, NOT proof of correctness — it asserts that a run today reproduces what was measured today. `match_mode: parent` rows are excluded from conformance numerators.

frameworks.note: 5 of our 65 ids are not real TSC criteria (CC6.9, CC7.6, CC9.3, A1.4, C1.3) — TSC 2017 stops at CC6.8/CC7.5/CC9.2/A1.3/C1.2. The crosswalk doubles as a library validator.

Our library is Annex-A only. Bound to BOTH sources: ISO 27001 2022 covers only management clauses 4-10 (51 SCF controls); ISO 27002 2022 is where Annex A lives (316). Bound to ISO 27002 ONLY: the ISO 27001 2022 key carries management clauses 4-10 whose bare numbers collide with Annex A after strip_prefix:A.
SCF carries 518 enhancement codes (AC-02(01)); our library is base controls only, so enhancements collapse to their base.
Our library is R2; SCF also carries R3. Upgrading the library is decision D2.
Our library is v8.0, SCF maps 8.1. Safeguard numbering is stable between them.
Library self-declares as synthetic paraphrase — the CODES are right, the TEXT is placeholder. Healthy crosswalk over unusable content.
KNOWN OVERCLAIM. Our 40 objectives are string prefixes of SCF's 230 practice-level codes (APO01 -> APO01.01..07). Navigation only; parent rows never enter a conformance numerator.
control_id is a local 1..n counter; the real clause lives in original_reference.
SCF writes Article 5.1(a), we write Article 5(1)(a). Flattening every paren on both sides makes them agree.
control_id is DORA-5.1; the citable article is original_reference (Article 5(1)).
SCF writes '§ 164.306' with a space, ours has none — symmetric normalization cancels it.
Library repaired: ids from 3.2 onward carried the wrong control's title/text against published CSCF v2024.

Library re-extracted: 170 rows with 81 unique ids (20 literally 'N/A') replaced by 71 uniquely-keyed subdomain rows. Our re-extracted ids are more granular than SCF's (3.1.4.7 vs 3.1.4), so sub-requirements roll up to their parent's mapping.
SCF's US SOX key is only 4 controls / 17 requirements. Ours is an ITGC set (APD-nn), not the statute. Expect ~zero and render mapped_control_count on the tile so it does not read as broken.

Library rebuilt from NIST's CSF 2.0 Reference Tool export (public domain US Government work) via grc.tools.build_nist_csf_library. Our 106 subcategory codes and SCF's nist_csf_20 agree exactly - no normalization beyond whitespace, no parent/child rollup.
No SCF key (HITRUST licences restrictively). HITRUST CSF is ISO 27002-derived — bridge each 00.a/01.a control to an ISO 27002 clause, then inherit SCF through the verified 27002 mapping.
UAE ADHICS is ISO 27002-derived; its HR/AM/AC section codes map cleanly to 27002 clauses.
Our single largest library (516 controls). Highest-value bridge target.
original_reference carries a domain label ('Governance B.3'), not a clause — check whether the source PDF cites ISO clauses before generating a mapping.
Data-management domains (DG/DQ/DC), not a security control set. Hand-curate to SCF DCH-* / PRI-* rather than bridging via 27002.
21 articles on cross-border transfer — hand-curate to SCF PRI-* (privacy) and DCH-* (data handling).

DO NOT auto-map to SCF's 'EMEA Saudi Arabia SACS-002 2022' on name similarity. SACS-002 is the underlying standard (SCF codes it VII.A.TPC-1..124); CCC is the certification scheme over it. 0/35 code overlap.
Occupational health & safety — out of SCF's scope by design. Keep native, map nothing.
frameworks.disposition_reason: ISO 45001 is an occupational health and safety management standard. It is outside the security/privacy control catalogue by design - SCF carries no crosswalk for it and no SCF control implements an OH&S obligation. Every requirement is dispositioned out_of_scope rather than left as a gap; covering it would need a separate, platform-authored OH&S control set.

frameworks.note: Library self-declares as synthetic pipeline-test content. Exclude from the canonical catalog (decision D7).
